data.text:
The SEO blog content has been completed for the Williams Painting Service website.

### Deliverables Completed:

- 15 fully written SEO-optimized blog articles (approximately 22,000–25,000 words total)
- Content optimized for local SEO targeting **Branson** and **Table Rock Lake**
- Service-focused blogs covering:
  - Interior Painting
  - Exterior Painting
  - Cabinet Refinishing
  - Deck Staining
  - Power Washing
  - Limewash Painting
- Educational and evergreen content to improve topical authority
- Conversion-focused articles with FAQs and strong calls-to-action

### SEO Optimization Required Before Publishing:

- Assign a primary keyword and supporting secondary keywords to each blog.
- Create SEO title tags (50–60 characters) and meta descriptions (150–160 characters).
- Optimize URL slugs.
- Add internal links to relevant service pages and other blog posts.
- Add 2–3 authoritative external links where appropriate.
- Upload optimized featured images with descriptive ALT text.
- Implement BlogPosting, FAQ, Breadcrumb, and Organization schema.
- Add a clickable Table of Contents for longer articles.
- Optimize readability with proper H1, H2, H3 hierarchy, short paragraphs, and bullet points.
- Ensure all images are compressed (WebP preferred) and pages are mobile-friendly.
- Submit the updated XML sitemap to Google Search Console and request indexing for each published blog.
- Verify Core Web Vitals and page speed after publishing.

### Post-Publishing Tasks:

- Share each blog on Google Business Profile and social media platforms.
- Monitor keyword rankings, impressions, CTR, organic traffic, and user engagement in Google Search Console and Google Analytics.
- Update internal links as new content is published to strengthen topical authority.

These blogs are intended to improve organic rankings, build topical authority, increase local visibility, and generate long-term organic traffic and qualified leads for the website.

data.text:
Hi Sam,

I prefer the version 2 of the website. Here are some requested changes.

Updated Website Structure

Since this is a startup business and we are only building three pages initially, I would like to simplify the website and focus on trust, products, and customer communication.

PAGE 1 – HOME

Purpose:

Introduce Hoku Labs, build trust, explain what makes us different, and direct visitors to the product page.

Sections:

1. Hero Section

- Hoku Labs logo

- Premium black and gold design

- Headline focused on transparency and value

- Shop Products button

1. Why Hoku Labs

- Direct manufacturer sourcing

- Competitive pricing

- Small-batch inventory

- Personalized customer service

- Available third-party testing

- Fast communication

1. Featured Products

- Retatrutide

- Tesamorelin

- MOTS-C

- NAD+

1. Available Testing / COA Section

- Show available COAs and testing documents

- Only display testing that actually exists

- Do not state all products or batches are tested

1. About Hoku Labs

   Short founder story emphasizing:

- Small business

- Direct sourcing

- Transparency

- Personalized customer support

- Lower overhead and pricing

1. Contact CTA

   "Questions? Contact us directly."

1. Required Research Disclaimer

   Place near bottom of page

\---

PAGE 2 – PRODUCTS

Purpose:

Allow customers to browse products and submit an order request.

Instead of a traditional e-commerce checkout, I would like a Request Order system.  But I am interested in a e commerce checkout system and am looking for a company that I can do the through for credit card transactions.

Each product should include:

- Product image

- Product name

- Price

Examples:

Retatrutide

10mg, 20mg, 30mg, 60mg

Tesamorelin

10mg, 20mg

MOTS-C

10mg, 20mg, 40mg

Etc.

Customer Workflow:

- Select products

- Add desired quantities

- Add to cart

- Submit Order Request

The order request should send:

- Customer name

- Email

- Phone number

- Selected products

- Quantities

This request should be emailed directly to me.

I will then contact the customer with payment instructions and fulfillment information.

This allows flexibility while payment processing is still being finalized.

\---

PAGE 3 – CONTACT / ORDER SUPPORT

Purpose:

Provide direct communication options.

Include:

Contact Information

- Email

- Phone

- Business hours

Payment Methods Accepted

Currently accepted:

- Venmo

- Cash App

- Zelle

- Apple Pay

- PayPal

- Bank Wire Transfer

- Cryptocurrency

FAQ Section

Examples:

- Do you provide COAs?

- How quickly do orders ship?

- What payment methods do you accept?

- How should products be stored?

Contact Form

- Name

- Email

- Message

Messages should be sent directly to my email.

\---

DESIGN DIRECTION

Overall design should feel:

- Premium

- Modern

- Black and gold

- Clean

- Luxury branding

Please avoid making the website look like a generic research chemical website.

I want it to feel like a boutique premium brand focused on transparency, customer service, and quality..

## **Website User Flow — Movie Subscription System**

### **1️⃣ User Visits Website**

User comes to the website and selects a movie to watch.

---

### **2️⃣ Free Preview (5–6 Minutes)**

When the movie starts:

- User can watch the first **5–6 minutes for free**.

---

### **3️⃣ Movie Pauses Automatically**

After 5–6 minutes:

- The movie **stops automatically**.
- A message appears on screen:

> **"To continue watching this movie, please subscribe."**

---

### **4️⃣ Subscription Prompt**

On the screen show:

- Subscription message
- Price: **$X**
- **Subscribe / Pay Now** button

---

### **5️⃣ User Makes Payment**

User clicks **Subscribe** and completes payment using available payment methods.

---

### **6️⃣ Access Unlocked**

After successful payment:

- User is redirected back to the movie.
- The movie continues from where it stopped.
- User can now **watch the full movie without any restriction**.

---

### **7️⃣ Subscription Status Saved**

User’s subscription status is saved in the system so:

- Next time they visit, they can watch movies without interruption (based on plan).

We are a licensed electrical contractor providing professional electrical services for:

**10. Please detail anything that you specifically do not want to have on your website.**

- ‌
- Cluttered hero sections or distracting animations – Don't overload the homepage with too many sliders, video popups, or homepage effects that distract from our core messaging.
- Unclear messaging or vague buzzwords – Avoid generic phrases like "synergy" or "cutting-edge solutions" that don't clearly explain what we do. Messaging should be precise and outcome-oriented.
- Overwhelming navigation or too many menu items – Keep the menu streamlined (Home, About, Services, Solutions, Case Studies, Contact). No sidebar navigation or excessive dropdowns that confuse visitors.
- Walls of text – Long paragraphs make content hard to scan. Keep copy concise, broken into short blocks with headings and visuals.
- Hidden or hard-to-find CTAs – Every page should have a clear call-to-action ("Get in Touch," "Schedule a Call") in plain sight, not buried or passive.
- Outdated or low-quality imagery – No blurry, generic stock photos or mismatched image styles. Instead, use modern, high-quality visuals that align with branding.
- ‌
- Unsecured components (no SSL, no CAPTCHA, no backups) – Ensure trust and security are built in. Avoid missing standard protections like SSL encryption, contact form CAPTCHA, or backup tools.

lists.name: 1. Intake (New Client) - PM will add the project card with client details.

4. Blocked - PM will resolve the issues which is blocking for the production. and move this card back to in scope.
5. Production Web Design Phase - PH will move the card to ready for QA if the Design is done.
5{A}. Design Completed Waiting for  Client Review
6. Production  Logo Design Phase -  PH will move the card to ready for QA if the Design is done.

7. Production SMM -  PH will move the card to ready for QA if the Work is done.
8. Design Revisoin - QA or PM will put design revisions here
9. In Production (Design Accepts) -  PH will move the card to ready for QA if the Development is done.
10. Details Needed From Client - After taking detail PM will move card to prodcution. (If Needed, After QA verification)
11. Ready for QA - QA will detect issues in the work Once issues are detected QA will move the card to QA fixes
12. QA & Fixes – QA will verify the fix and move the card to Client Review if changes are made, or back to the relevant production phase if not.
13. Client Review - PM Will Provide the client review here and move the card back to the relevant production phase.(if revision are needed)
14. Approved from Client - PM Will move card If the client approves the work
15. Delivered ( Complete ) - PM Will Move Card if the work is delivered to the client
15{A}Hold By Client - Pm will move the card if the client holds the project
